1fb4b73e4c77f6596fb4a3335557f08474c42bc9: Colere is a small-scale, low-key resort — 21 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Difficult terrain is king at Colere: with 45 black and 55 red runs on offer, confident skiers will find plenty to challenge them. Off-piste and freeride are practised here in often excellent conditions, thanks to the altitude and the orientation of the slopes. Colere's altitude (1060 m at the bottom, 2178 m at the top) helps it keep a decent snow cover in midwinter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it's best to check conditions before finalising a booking. The day lift pass at €48 places Colere in the intermediate category on budget — neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and its facilities justifies this price for most skiers. In short: Colere doesn't rival the ski giants, and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

1fdc787ec0353af1bb0cb8ff7edcc76107c89a03: Human-scale resort, Saint-Gervais focuses on warm welcome and closeness rather than impressive figures. Its 45 km of runs are ideal for a 3–4 day stay, especially with family or for skiers who don't need to constantly change their playground. Saint-Gervais's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Its altitude (850 m at the bottom, 2350 m at the top) allows a decent snow cover in mid-winter. January and February are the most reliable; in December and March, it's worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. The budget for a stay in Saint-Gervais is clearly high: 59€ for a day pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before setting off. In short: Saint-Gervais is one of those rare resorts that combines a real village, a sincere family atmosphere and runs suited to everyone. Hard to get your stay wrong here.
